title: Decentralized control problems in neumann-economies
summary_en: Kornai and Simonovits develop a formal decentralised-control framework for John von Neumann's expanding-economy model. They study how a centrally planned economy in which sectoral managers respond to local price-and-quantity signals (rather than full information) can or cannot reach the von Neumann balanced-growth path. The mathematical analysis identifies conditions on price-adjustment rules and information lags under which the decentralised system converges, and characterises stability properties relevant to debates about market socialism that were active when the paper was published.
data_used: Theoretical model — no dataset. Builds on the von Neumann balanced-growth model, with explicit decentralised price- and quantity-adjustment rules.
policy_relevance: Foundational paper in the Hungarian School of mathematical economics on whether decentralised control can replicate centralised planning outcomes — directly relevant to the academic debate that informed Hungary's 1968 New Economic Mechanism and later transition discussions. Continued historical relevance for Hungarian economic-policy literacy and the KRTK's institutional self-understanding.
